clue.text: Unpleasant sound in old recording of ballet?

indicators.note: the word in tells us the sound sits inside the recording

parts.note: a cassette is an old-fashioned tape recording
noise is unwanted or unpleasant sound

explanation.surface: Someone complains of crackle on an old tape of a ballet score.
explanation.walkthrough: CASSE-NOISETTE is the French title of Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Casse-Noisette is the original French name of Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker ballet, so it is an example of a ballet.

clue.text: To dissect a very little matter is easy at first

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
an atom is a tiny particle of matter

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word easy

explanation.surface: Cutting up a tiny scrap is simple, at least to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To anatomise is to cut up a body to study its structure, which is to dissect it.

clue.text: It's monotonous to speak about setter

indicators.note: about tells us the word for speaking goes around the setter

parts.note: to say is to speak
the crossword setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter admits that talking about himself is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something samey is repetitive and unvarying, so it is monotonous.

clue.text: North Surrey growth centre

indicators.note: growth suggests letters developing into a new form, so Surrey is rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden centre in north Surrey where plants are grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth centre' reads like the whole definition, but with no other anagram signal in the clue, 'growth' has to do that job, leaving 'centre' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a centre where plants are raised or young children cared for.

clue.text: Not Abraham, but his male issue

definitions.text: Not Abraham, but his male issue

indicators.note: issue means to come out, so the letters of his male emerge in a new order

explanation.surface: It is not Abraham himself but his son who is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' doubles as offspring in the whole-clue reading: Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Ishmael is the firstborn son of Abraham, so he is Abraham's male offspring rather than Abraham.

clue.text: Oil — expert refiner can make it profitable

definitions.note: a phrase for a person who makes money from something, standing for a noun

indicators.note: a refiner processes crude material into a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An expert at refining oil can turn it into a money-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploiter is someone who uses a resource for gain, one who turns it to profit.

clue.text: Headdress for one in old Irish royal seat

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the name of the royal site

parts.note: the Hill of Tara was the seat of the ancient High Kings of Ireland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crown worn by someone at the ancient seat of Irish kings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a type of headdress.

clue.text: Hazard for the learned?

parts.note: to hazard is to venture an estimate; one made by a scholarly person, or an informed one, fits the phrase

explanation.surface: A danger that threatens academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' looks like a noun meaning danger, but it is the verb in 'hazard a guess'.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate based on knowledge is one ventured by someone schooled in the subject.

clue.text: For a long shot, not else to help develop

indicators.note: develop, as with photographs, signals the letters being worked into something new

explanation.surface: A photographer insists that only this will help develop a distant picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens magnifies distant subjects, used for taking long-range photographs.

clue.text: Lifeless month with a solemn air

parts.note: dead means lifeless
March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A gloomy month accompanied by a mournful tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead march is slow funeral music, a solemn tune; air here means a melody.

clue.text: Shalom, with a quarter in step

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the word for step

parts.note: a pace is a single step
E for east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A Hebrew greeting offered while walking in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalom is the Hebrew word for tranquillity, used as a greeting, and translates as this word.

clue.text: Nick with radiators in order? Unknown!

parts.note: CH stands for central heating, the system of radiators
OK means in order, all right
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether the radiators work in a police station cell.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOKY is British slang for prison; 'nick' is also British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British slang for a prison or jail.

clue.text: Are round table members complicated?

indicators.note: members are the component parts, so the letters are taken apart and reassembled

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about whether Arthur's knights are a tricky lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round table members' suggests King Arthur's knights; that picture is the misdirection, and 'members' (component parts) is only a loose anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate and detailed, hence complicated.

clue.text: Term with test contained in it?

indicators.note: contained signals that the following words sit inside the word for test

parts.note: to try is to test

explanation.surface: A school term that includes an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: TRINITY term is the summer term at Oxford and some other universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is the name of a university term, the summer one at Oxford and Dublin.

clue.text: Soundly conclude to get a girl to hospital

indicators.note: soundly tells us the word for conclude is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to infer is to conclude
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone decides they must get a young woman to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a place caring for the sick, a hospital.

clue.text: Language sounding like a vegetable when drunk

indicators.note: sounding like says the vegetable's name is pronounced, here with a drunken slur

parts.note: lettuce is a salad vegetable

explanation.surface: A tongue that sounds like a salad leaf to a tipsy speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' explains the slurred pronunciation of LETTUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is an old name for Latvian, the language of Latvia.

clue.text: No one can get a nickel to overturn lassitude

indicators.note: in a down entry, to overturn is to turn the whole run upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tin is a can
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: Weariness so great nobody can tip over a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' reverses the whole string NOITINANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanition is exhaustion from lack of nourishment, hence weariness or lassitude.

clue.text: Abstruse playwright working for a chippie

definitions.note: a phrase for what a chip shop cook does, standing for the verb

parts.note: deep means profound, abstruse
Christopher Fry was an English playwright

explanation.surface: A difficult dramatist takes a job in a fish and chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippie is British slang for a fish-and-chip shop, where food is cooked in hot fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking food immersed in hot oil is the main job done in a fish-and-chip shop.

clue.text: Maynard's confection for one in the Met?

indicators.note: a confection is something mixed up, so the letters of the name are recombined

parts.note: Maynards is a British sweet maker, and its name is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet from Maynards made for a London policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police, headquartered at Scotland Yard, so a Yard man is one of its detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yard man is a detective from Scotland Yard, headquarters of the Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Fruit said to be in season?

indicators.note: said means the word for in season is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: current means present, of the moment, in season

explanation.surface: A fruit described as being in season.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape or a berry, a fruit.

clue.text: Mark up everything at the beginning of the month

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everything
1 Dec, written I DEC, is the beginning of the month of December

explanation.surface: Prices are raised across the board on the first of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is a diacritical mark placed under a letter such as c.

clue.text: Where a platter may be spoken of as "not one of us"?

indicators.note: spoken of signals that the position of the platter is heard rather than written

parts.note: a platter may sit under bread

explanation.surface: A snob describes an outsider using a dining-table image.
explanation.definitionFit: Underbred means ill-bred, of low breeding, which a snob means by calling someone not one of us.

clue.text: Church teaching could make you go mad

indicators.note: could make you suggests the letters can be made into something else

explanation.surface: Religious doctrine might drive a person insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by a church as true.

clue.text: Which fabric to use, time will tell

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Only time will tell which cloth to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a woven cloth with diagonal ribs, a fabric.

clue.text: Go on the street to arrange to meet

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone goes out on the street to fix a rendezvous.
explanation.definitionFit: To tryst, as a verb, is to make an appointment, especially a lovers' meeting.

clue.text: A classic car is back, of classic character

indicators.note: back means the run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: MG is a classic British sports car make
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vintage car returns, full of old-fashioned charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses AMGIS; 'classic' in the definition means Greek, the classical language.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is a letter, or character, of the Greek alphabet, Greek being a classical language.

clue.text: Mother seduces chap from the Far East …

parts.note: ma is mother
lays, in slang, means has sex with, seduces
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A mother leads astray a man from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaysia lies in South-East Asia, so a Malaysian person comes from the Far East.

clue.text: … an expectant mother?

parts.note: a pregnant woman is someone waiting for a baby, read as a royal attendant's title

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman, following on from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's seductive mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant woman is literally a lady who is waiting, playing on the royal attendant's title.
